locations.name: Cerberus-Hades
locations.card:
Hades, a neutron star orbiting Delta Pavonis as a distant twin, was converted long ago into an
enormous computer. Cerberus, the artificial planet orbiting it, is its gate; the expedition of
2567 entered it, and Dan Sylveste remains.

locations.name: Surtsey
locations.card:
A Pattern Juggler world. Dan Sylveste swam here as a young man, before the Shroud expedition
made his name.

687's second planet for the map.

locations.name: Yellowstone
locations.card:
A terrestrial planet, habitable in patches thanks to gases from a deep chasm.

**Condition over time**

- 2350–2510: thriving — Belle Époque
- 2510–present: degraded — Post-plague

locations.name: Wintersea
locations.card:
A Pattern Juggler world. The Nostalgia for Infinity called here; her second-in-command
Sajaki drowned, and Captain Brannigan secretly overwrote his mind.
SYSTEM IS A PLACEHOLDER: canon does not locate Wintersea; pinned to Ross 248, a system with
no other modelled events, pending a canon fix.

locations.name: Santiago
locations.card: One of the five Flotilla ships — with Palestine, Brasilia, Islamabad and Baghdad — that left Mercury in 2083 for the 61 Cygni A system: humanity's first manned interstellar colonisation effort. Each was a two-kilometre re-purposed in-system freighter carrying 960 passengers in reefersleep caskets and a crew of 150, driven by a lithium/antilithium reaction with separate antimatter reservoirs for acceleration and deceleration. The destination planet was named Journey's End and renamed Sky's Edge by the colonists. Only three of the five reached it, undone by external sabotage and internal scheming; the Santiago was one of them, and Schuyler 'Sky' Haussmann sailed aboard her. DATES ARE APPROXIMATE: 2083 is the official departure, but the official timeline says only that the Flotilla would not arrive before the twenty-third century, so 2300 stands for the LATEST possible arrival rather than a documented one. The ship's own fate after arrival is not modelled.

people.name: Bernsdottir
people.bio: Discovered the first Shroud in 2338, thirty-five years before Lascaille's encounter made them infamous.

people.name: Calvin Sylveste
people.bio:
Yellowstone magnate of the Sylveste dynasty. Cloned himself and raised the clone as his son,
Dan; commissioned an alpha-level simulation of his mind; then died as one of the Eighty
(~2372). The son and the simulation both outlived him. Dates approximate.

people.name: Demarchists
people.bio: Democratic anarchy. The Belle Époque was their era.

people.name: Greenfly
people.bio: Human-designed terraforming swarm; by 40,000 AD it had restructured vast swathes of the Milky Way.

people.name: Ice Mendicants
people.bio: Charitable medical order in orbit around Yellowstone; they ran the hospices of the Rust Belt.

people.name: Ilia Volyova
people.bio: Triumvir of the Nostalgia for Infinity and keeper of its cache of hell-class weapons. Aboard since well before the Resurgam affair; her exact join year is unrecorded.

people.name: Inhibitors
people.bio: Post-intelligent machine race from the Dawn War, galaxy-scale in intent. Called wolves by the Conjoiners.

people.name: Irravel Veda
people.bio: Pilot of the Galactic North thread. Recloned from herself in 2673, she fought a relativistic vendetta across centuries, and in 2931 met a representative of the Nestbuilder intelligence.

people.name: John Brannigan
people.bio:
Captain of the Nostalgia for Infinity, later quarantined in a reefersleep tank as the melding
plague slowly transformed him and merged him with his own ship. At the Juggler world
Wintersea (~2500) he secretly overwrote his drowned second-in-command Sajaki with a copy
of his mind. Dates approximate.

people.name: Panoply
people.bio: Elite law enforcement of the Demarchist regime; the police force for the Glitter Band.

people.name: Pattern Jugglers
people.bio:
Aquatic alien minds dissolved across the oceans of many worlds, trading in thoughts and
memories. Humans who swim among them risk conjoinment — or worse. Known Juggler worlds
include Surtsey, Turquoise, Wintersea and Ararat.

people.name: Sandra Voi
people.bio: Led the first human expedition into Europa's ocean (2161); brokered the ceasefire that ended the Coalition–Conjoiner war (2191).

people.name: Sky Haussmann
people.bio: Schuyler 'Sky' Haussmann — a 'momio', a sleeper awakened from reefersleep, who sailed on the Santiago. He jettisoned reefersleep caskets so the Santiago would arrive first at Journey's End, and the colonists renamed the planet 'Sky's Edge' as a mockery. Crucified through a stand-in, he slept a century in reefersleep, and became the centre of the Church of Sky cult and its indoctrination virus. He re-emerged as the arms dealer Cahuella, then as 'Tanner Mirabel', then as 'H' — the man who killed and replaced the Mademoiselle, and who drew Nevil Clavain into the Resurgam evacuation. Immortal; his death date is not established. DATES ARE APPROXIMATE: the official timeline fixes the Flotilla's 2083 departure and says it would not arrive before the twenty-third century, so 2300 stands in for the latest possible arrival at Sky's Edge; 2517 is the year Tanner Mirabel reaches Chasm City, by which point the Mirabel/Reivich sequence has played out. He was certainly in Chasm City by 2524, when he recruited Ana Khouri into Shadowplay. The Flotilla years (2083-2300) are not modelled — there is no node for the Santiago.

people.name: Yuuji Sajaki
people.bio:
Second-in-command of the Nostalgia for Infinity under Captain Brannigan. Drowned at the
Juggler world Wintersea (~2500); Brannigan secretly overwrote his mind with a copy of his
own. As "Sajaki" he served as triumvir through the Resurgam affair and commanded the 2566
abduction of Dan Sylveste.

events.title: Amerikano era — Von Neumann colonies beyond Sol.
events.card: Fertilised human cells seeded extrasolar worlds by robot. Most such colonies collapsed within two or three generations.

events.title: Bernsdottir discovers the first Shroud.
Expedition into the Cerberus/Hades artefact; death of Dan Sylveste.
events.card: Hades, a neutron star orbiting Delta Pavonis as a distant twin, was converted long ago into an enormous computer. The crew of the Nostalgia for Infinity entered Cerberus, the artificial planet guarding it. Sylveste remained.

events.title: Clavain defects from the Conjoiners.
events.card: The break that precedes the exploitation of grub technology, including inertia suppression machinery.

events.title: Clavain's return from deep space.
Confrontation between Clavain and Volyova around Delta Pavonis.
events.card: A standoff over the Nostalgia for Infinity and her cache of doomsday weapons; the ship leaves for deep space after.

events.title: Great Wall of Mars begins; the Coalition for Neural Purity forms.
events.card: An Earth-based military pact of conservative states, opposed to the neural experimentation the Demarchists tolerated. The first phase of the Great Wall of Mars was completed in 2182.

events.title: Conjoiner–Demarchist war around Yellowstone.
events.card: Ended by the Ferrisville Convention.

events.title: Galiana's Conjoiners escape Mars; first relativistic starship.
events.card: Escape from quarantine aboard the first starship launched from Mars orbit. It opens the great interstellar expansion of 2205–2250.

events.title: Conjoiner quarantine.
events.card: Sandra Voi brokers the ceasefire that ends the Coalition–Conjoiner war; the Conjoiners are quarantined on Mars for fourteen years.

events.title: Emergence of Demarchist states.
events.card: After three decades of turmoil, the Demarchist settlement of the solar system begins; by 2155 their habitats ring Jupiter while the Great freeze closes over Earth.

events.title: Denizen uprising; fall of the Europan cities.
Conjoiner expedition to Diadem; Setterholm's Worms.
events.card: Diadem is not charted here. The worms found beneath its ice are the subject of the story Glacial.

events.title: Hostage crisis around Fand.
Departure of the Flotilla from Mercury.
events.card: Ceasefire in the system wars. Five generation ships — Santiago, Palestine, Brasilia, Islamabad and Baghdad — leave Mercury for 61 Cygni A at an eighth of lightspeed, arriving no sooner than the twenty-third century.

events.title: Departure of Galiana and Clavain's expedition into deep space.
events.card: Departure point not pinned to a specific body.

events.title: Galiana's return from deep space.
events.card: Returned terminally injured, aboard a stolen Conjoiner ship.

events.title: Emergence of the Green Wave
events.card: Systematic dismantling of many solar systems. Greenfly is a human-designed terraforming machine, a swarm of Von Neumann robots programmed to break apart terrestrial planets and make them habitable. It began adapting, started classifying intelligent life as a threat, and by 40,000 had transformed vast swathes of the Milky Way.

events.title: Events of the human-Inhibitor war
events.card: The Inhibitors are a galaxy-scale threat: a post-intelligent machine race left over from the Dawn War, whose stated purpose was to inhibit the spread of intelligent life beyond individual planets or solar systems ahead of the Andromeda–Milky Way collision. Called wolves by the Conjoiners because they lurked in the blackness of interstellar space and attacked in packs.

events.title: Ana Khouri arrives in Chasm City.
Philip Lascaille's encounter with the Shroud in the Trans Tau Ceti sector.
Melding Plague afflicts Chasm City; effective end of Demarchist era.
Tanner Mirabel arrives in Chasm City.
Irravel Veda meets a representative of the Nestbuilder intelligence.
events.card: The Nestbuilders, the hidden civilisation of this region, have been watching what is coming.

events.title: Arrival of the Nostalgia for Infinity in the p Eridani system.
events.card: The 61 Cygni system. Survivors of the Resurgam years found refuge on Ararat.

events.title: departure of Resurgam expedition.
Shiva-Parvati cordon crisis.
Abduction of Dan Sylveste from Resurgam.
events.card: Taken by the lighthugger Nostalgia for Infinity, under triumvir Sajaki.

events.title: Calvin Sylveste commissions an alpha-level simulation of his mind.
events.card:
A perfect alpha-level copy of Calvin's mind, recorded shortly before he joined the Eighty's
destructive upload attempt. The upload failed, as all eighty did; the simulation survived,
passing to Dan — who ran it on Resurgam two centuries later as he worked to decode the
Amarantin archive.

events.title: Dan Sylveste born in Chasm City — Calvin's clone, passed off as his son.
events.card:
Publicly the son and heir of Yellowstone magnate Calvin Sylveste; in truth a clone of Calvin
himself, created as his continuation and raised as his natural child. Dan learned the truth
only decades later.

events.title: Departure of Sylveste expedition to Lascaille's Shroud.
Return of Sylveste's expedition to Lascaille's Shroud.
Dan Sylveste swims with the Pattern Jugglers at Surtsey.
events.card:
As a young man, before the Shroud expedition made his name, Sylveste travelled to the
Juggler world Surtsey and entered the water — one of the few humans to swim among the
Pattern Jugglers and come back. The experience marked him, and coloured what he was later
able to read from alien minds.
DATE IS APPROXIMATE: placed before the 2405 Shroud departure.

events.title: Dan Sylveste vanishes from Yellowstone for 30 days.
The Eighty — failed mind uploads on Yellowstone.
events.card:
Eighty of Yellowstone's wealthiest paid for the first destructive mind uploads. All eighty
scanned patterns emerged corrupt, and the originals died in the process. Calvin Sylveste
was among them; the alpha-level simulation of his mind, made shortly beforehand, was all
that survived.

events.title: Transenlightenment on Mars; the Conjoiners are born.
events.card: Experimenters under the Great Wall initiate the Transenlightenment; the Coalition–Conjoiner war begins at once.

events.title: Irravel Veda recloned from herself.
events.card: The Galactic North thread — a pilot restored from her own tissue, resuming a relativistic vendetta against Mirsky.

events.title: Sandra Voi leads the first expedition into Europa's ocean.
Arrival of the lighthugger Voice of Evening around Turquoise.
events.card: A rare visitor to a backwoods world, and its main link to the rest of the volume.

events.title: The Nostalgia for Infinity at Wintersea; Brannigan overwrites Sajaki.
events.card:
The lighthugger Nostalgia for Infinity called at the Juggler world Wintersea. Yuuji Sajaki,
second-in-command under Captain John Brannigan, drowned in a Juggler swim — and Brannigan,
already succumbing to the melding plague, secretly overwrote his mind with a copy of his
own. From then on "Sajaki" was Brannigan's continuation, and it was "Sajaki" who commanded
the abduction of Dan Sylveste from Resurgam.
DATE IS APPROXIMATE: the novel fixes no year; the visit must predate the ship's 2520s
Yellowstone stop. The system is a placeholder — see Wintersea.
